title: Slate: hierarchical lane + micro-lens workspace switcher proposal
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our current console navigation creates cognitive load for users who manage multiple workspaces and need quick context (model, route, cost lens). Existing sidebar variants are too flat for teams that switch contexts frequently and want route-preserving switching for rollouts and cost analysis.

Proposal: Introduce a 'Slate' navigation pattern: a hierarchical lane (left rail) that groups contextual surfaces into lanes, plus a compact micro-lens workspace switcher embedded in the rail header. Key ideas: progressive disclosure of lanes, route preservation on workspace switch, inline cost badges per lane, presence indicators for active rollouts, and route-aware breadcrumbs that surface which model/route is pinned to a workspace.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-switch between workspaces and routes by 40% in common workflows (dashboards, rollouts, cost view).
- Preserve user route state where possible during workspace switching (e.g., stay on the same dashboard route if it exists in target workspace).
- Surface per-route cost and SLO signals directly in navigation to encourage cost-aware routing.
- Offer a compact switcher for keyboard-first users and a detailed explorer for power users.

Design deliverables included here: low-fi wireframes, interactive Figma prototype for the Slate rail and micro-lens switcher, accessibility notes, and a rollout plan that enables canary exposure and metrics collection (switch success rate, bounce-to-home, average time-to-task).

Acceptance criteria:
- Visual spec and Figma prototype reviewed by PM and Eng and approved for handoff.
- Implementation checklist with feature flags and telemetry events defined.
- Usability test with 8 participants shows improvement in task completion for workspace switching tasks.
- Dev-ready tokens and CNAMES for sidebar variants included in the handoff package.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Maya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Decided to prioritize route preservation and visible cost badges over early compact variant. Action: design to produce 3 variations (accordion lane, stacked lane, micro-lens) by 2025-02-21.

2025-02-21 - Liam Chen: Delivered three explorations in Figma (links below). Engineering feasibility review flagged concerns about maintaining KV cache mapping across workspaces; Eng recommends a graceful fallback that preserves query params where model route doesn't exist.

2025-02-25 - PM Review (Sofia Ramirez): Prefer the accordion lane with inline cost lenses. Request: add an admin toggle to hide cost badges for private deployments. Also ask for telemetry event names to match conventions (nav.switch, nav.lane_click, nav.workspace_switch_attempt).

2025-02-28 - Design critique: Accessibility review requests larger hit targets for micro-lens controls and ARIA labels for presence indicator chips. Action: update prototype and include a11y checklist in handoff.

2025-03-02 - Engineering (Anita Gupta): Confirmed routing rules for route-preserve behavior. Added dependency ENG-3842 for runtime routing API. Suggested adding a fallback UX that surfaces 'Route not available in target workspace — open home/dashboard instead?'

2025-03-03 - Liam Chen: Merged final prototype into design handoff bundle and submitted PRD to Confluence. Ready for PM signoff and to schedule a 2-week canary with 5% of org users behind a feature flag.
